bug_semantics: Authenticated users with leads access can inject arbitrary SQL into a HAVING clause of the leads DataGrid. LeadDataGrid::prepareQueryBuilder() builds a computed rotten_lead alias via CASE/DATEDIFF, then concatenates request()->input('rotten_lead.in') (the rotten_lead[in] query parameter) into havingRaw() with no binding, cast, or allowlist. That raw HAVING string is executed as SQL, enabling boolean- and time-based blind extraction of the full database (credential hashes, CRM records, config).
flaw_origin: The sink was first written on 2022-08-31 in non-merge commit f344238f734bcba261a885870ba9d205fb8aeccf ('added rotten lead filter') by prabhat gautam as part of PR #1068 (Fixed #764). That commit introduced both the computed rotten_lead SELECT alias and the unparameterized havingRaw('rotten_lead = ' . request()->input('rotten_lead.in')) call. Later commits only added a table-prefix and formatting; they did not create the injection. The parent tree has no havingRaw and no rotten_lead.in filter.
